beam_energy.note: Added 2026-09-17. This is the SLC linac's quoted maximum per-beam energy, not the energy actually used for physics: to sit on the Z resonance the collider ran at cms/2 ~ 45.5-45.6 GeV per beam (see this record's cms_energy, ~91 GeV / Z mass). Both figures come from the same Wikipedia article; sourced to Wikipedia only, confidence uncertain per A17.
beam_energy.quote: an RF linear accelerator that accelerated electrons and positrons up to 50 GeV

cms_energy.note: Sourced to Wikipedia only ('about 90 GeV, equal to the mass of the Z boson'); recorded as ~91 GeV (the Z mass) with approx flag.
cms_energy.quote: The center of mass energy was about 90 GeV, equal to the mass of the Z boson, which the accelerator was designed to study.

summary.plain: A particle collider at SLAC that smashed together beams of electrons and positrons tuned to the mass of the Z boson, letting physicists study that particle's properties with the SLD detector from 1989 to 1998.
summary.technical: Stanford Linear Collider: SLAC's linac accelerated electrons and positrons (up to 50 GeV per beam by design) around a single-pass arc to collide at the Z resonance (~91 GeV cms, ~45.5 GeV/beam), studied by the SLD detector, 1989-1998.
